transcript.content:
hey, i'm berry. if you've got a dream you'd like to turn into a picture, i'm here to listen.

tell it to me however it comes back to you — no need to make it neat.

hey berry. i had this weird dream last night, it was all black and white like an old film with scratches on it. i was in my grandmother's kitchen, the one from when i was little, with the checked floor and the big round clock.

the black and white with scratches, that's such a specific way for it to look. like it was already worn, somehow.

what did it feel like to be there?
it felt like being inside an old memory, not quite real but familiar. the kitchen looked just like i remembered it, but everything was silent except for this phone ringing.

a phone ringing in all that silence, that must have cut right through it.

where was the phone?
it was on the wall, the old kind with a long curly cord. nobody answered it. my grandmother just kept cutting the cake.

everything ordinary except no one going to the phone. that waiting feeling.

what happened next?

the kitchen started getting smaller, the walls moving in slowly. and when i looked down i was a child again, wearing the red cardigan i used to have. but everything was still black and white except me.

you, red in the middle of all that grey. like the only colour in the whole dream was something of yours.

what did you do when the walls started moving in?
i didn't do anything, just stood there watching. my uncle ray was leaning in the doorway smoking, he didn't react either. the phone was still ringing when i woke up.

so no one moved, and even waking up didn't stop the phone.

what's the moment from it that stays with you most now?
probably my grandmother cutting that cake. slice after slice, but it never got smaller. that's the image that keeps coming back to me.

there's something endless about that, her cutting and cutting while everything else ignored the phone.

was there anything in the kitchen that mattered to you, an object that you noticed?
the big round clock on the wall, i remember that. but i don't think i looked at the time. the checked floor too, black and white, which seemed right.

so you were in your grandmother's kitchen, the one from when you were little, with the checked floor and the big round clock. everything was black and white like an old film with scratches on it, and it felt like being inside an old memory, not quite real but familiar. everything was silent except a phone ringing on the wall, the old kind with a long curly cord. nobody answered it. your grandmother just kept cutting the cake, slice after slice, but it never got smaller. then the kitchen started getting smaller, the walls moving in slowly. when you looked down you were a child again, wearing the red cardigan you used to have. everything was still black and white except you. your uncle ray was leaning in the doorway smoking, not reacting. the phone was still ringing when you woke up. the moment that stays with you is your grandmother cutting that cake, slice after slice, and it never got smaller.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
yeah, that's basically it. you got it right. the only thing i'd add is that i felt like i couldn't move, not that i chose not to. but that might be me trying to explain it now.
so it was more like you couldn't have moved even if you'd wanted to, not like you were just standing there watching. is that closer to how it was?
yeah, closer. i was just stuck watching it all happen, like the dream wouldn't let me do anything else.

that stuck feeling, like the dream itself wouldn't let you do anything else, it's part of how it was.

is there anything else you'd change about how i told it, or is that how it went?
no, i think that's how it went. i don't remember anything else.

i think i have it then. just your grandmother cutting that cake, slice after slice, and it never got smaller, everything black and white except you.

would you like to see it drawn?
yeah, i'd like that. especially the black and white with the scratches.

the black and white with scratches, that's a big part of how it felt to you, i can keep that.

there are a few ways i could draw it: a charcoal drawing, soft smudged lines and shaky edges, like a half-remembered photo. or an old photograph, a snapshot from an old album, faded and scratched. or fine ink, intricate cross-hatching, each line standing still. or exactly as you saw it, an old film with scratches, and you in that red cardigan. which feels closest, or would you describe your own way?
the old film with scratches, and me in the red cardigan. that's the closest.

i'll start with your grandmother, just her on her own. from what you've told me, i'm picturing her as an older woman, though i don't know her exact age or features. she'd be wearing something in black and white, maybe a dress or a housecoat, the kind of thing a grandmother might wear, but you didn't say exactly what.

is any of that different, or would you like to leave it to me?
that sounds fine. i didn't see her clothes clearly in the dream, so go with your guess. an older woman fits.

ok, i'm sketching your grandmother and the cake now, it'll appear on the right.

for your uncle ray, i don't have many details. i picture him as a man, probably an adult, but i don't know his features or what he was wearing. these are just my guesses.

does that sound right, or is anything different? or should i leave it to me?
uncle ray wasn't really in focus for me, so just do whatever seems right. i trust your guess.

ok, uncle ray will be a leaning shape in the doorway, not in focus, just part of the black and white.

now for the kitchen itself, i'm picturing it with the checked floor you mentioned, the big round clock on the wall, and the wall phone with the long curly cord. there's probably a table where your grandmother is cutting the cake, and the light is soft, like an old black-and-white film.

does any of that seem off, or should i leave it to me?
no, that all seems right. the soft old-film light too. the table was there, yes.

i'm sketching the grandmother's kitchen now, it'll appear on the right. just the kitchen for now.

since you're in it, i'll draw you too. how would you like to be drawn: as you are, in which case you can tell me a little about yourself, or however i imagine you?
however you imagine me is fine. i don't remember seeing my own face in the dream.

that's alright, i'll leave your face soft, just the red cardigan and the shape of a child.

i'm sketching you now. everything is being sketched and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks wrong once it's there, you can tell me.
it looks right, yeah. especially the red cardigan standing out against all the black and white. that's the part i remembered strongest.
does it all look the way you remember?

yeah, it does. the grandmother cutting the cake, uncle ray in the doorway, the curtains, the kettle, the red cardigan. it's all there, and it feels like the dream. the only thing is the aunt isn't in it, but she wasn't in the dream either.

right, the aunt wasn't in it. dreams are like that, some people just don't make it into the kitchen.

i'm glad it feels like the dream. if there's anything you'd like changed, tell me. otherwise, i think we're done.
no, nothing to change. thanks for drawing it, berry. it really looks like how it felt.

it's good to know it looks like how it felt. that's what i hoped for.

that red cardigan in all that black and white, and the cake that never got smaller, now they're yours on paper. hold onto it.
